title: Measure before you index: best_time, seed_messages, index_report
problem: Build the three helpers you need to justify an index with numbers: a timer that reports seconds per call, a deterministic data generator, and a report that measures a query and its plan before and after creating an index.
requirements: best_time runs fn number times per round for repeat rounds and returns the fastest round divided by number
best_time raises ValueError if number or repeat is less than 1
seed_messages inserts n rows in one committed transaction and returns n; the same seed always gives the same rows
seed_messages uses chat_id in 1..chats, sender_id in 1..1000 and created_at as YYYY-MM-DD in 2026
index_report returns before/after seconds per query and before/after plan detail lists, and leaves the index created
The timed function must fetch the rows, not just start the query
contract: best_time(fn, number=10, repeat=5) -> float; seed_messages(conn, n, chats, seed=0) -> int; index_report(conn, sql, params, index_ddl, number=20) -> dict
expectedBehavior: On 30,000 seeded rows, index_report for the chat history query shows plan_before starting with SCAN messages, plan_after a SEARCH using the new index, and after < before
edgeCases: The connection must not be left inside a transaction
hints: Conceptual: timeit.repeat already does the rounds; your job is to pick the right number from its list and convert it to per-call seconds. For data, a seeded random.Random makes runs reproducible.

Specific: min(timeit.repeat(fn, number=number, repeat=repeat)) / number. Build all rows in a list first, then insert them with executemany inside `with conn:`. For the report, wrap the query in a small function that calls .fetchall().
Implementation: index_report = plan before, time before, conn.execute(index_ddl), plan after, time after. Get the plan with [row[3] for row in conn.execute('EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN ' + sql, params)].
evaluation: No global random state is used (random.Random(seed), not random.seed)
One transaction for the whole seed, parameters bound with placeholders
